description: How long a file takes to download at your internet speed, or the speed you need. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

efficiencyPercent.description: How much of the line speed the download really gets, in percent. 100 is the pure arithmetic; real downloads usually reach 80-90 because of protocol overhead, Wi-Fi and the server's own limit.

size.description: The file size, in sizeUnit. Defaults to 50 (a 50 GB game).

sizeUnit.description: Unit of size. KB/MB/GB/TB are decimal (1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes, as stores and drive makers count); KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB are binary (1 GiB = 1,073,741,824 bytes, what Windows labels GB).

speed.description: The connection speed, in speedUnit. Defaults to 100 (Mbps). Ignored when timeSeconds is given.

speedUnit.description: Unit of speed. Kbps/Mbps/Gbps are bits per second, as internet plans are sold; MB/s is megabytes per second, as download managers show it. 1 MB/s = 8 Mbps.

timeSeconds.description: Reverse mode: the time the download may take, in seconds. Given, the answer is the line speed needed (in Mbps and MB/s) instead of a time, and speed is ignored.

name: download_time_calculator
title: Download Time Calculator
